questions.question: What is included in the agent-workbench-pack directory layout?
options: model weights, training data, eval scripts, deployment configs
AGENTS.md, docs/ (rules + policy + protocol + rubric), schemas/ (state + board + scope), scripts/ (init + feedback + verify + handoff), bin/install.sh
README.md, requirements.txt, src/, tests/, Dockerfile
config.yaml, tools/, memory/, prompts/, workflows/
questions.explanation: The pack layout: AGENTS.md, docs/ (agent-rules.md, reliability-policy.md, handoff-protocol.md, reviewer-rubric.md), schemas/ (agent_state, task_board, scope_contract schemas), scripts/ (init_agent.py, run_with_feedback.py, verify_agent.py, generate_handoff.py), bin/install.sh.

questions.question: What is the VERSION file's role and what triggers a major version bump?
options: VERSION tracks git commits; major bump on any code change
VERSION is the contract: major bumps for schema/script changes requiring migrations, minor for other changes, patch for doc-only changes
VERSION is for marketing purposes only
VERSION tracks the number of tasks completed
questions.explanation: VERSION is the contract. Major bumps: schema changes or script changes that require state migrations. Minor bumps: other changes requiring a checker re-run. Patch bumps: doc-only changes. The installer writes .workbench-version into the target repo; lint_pack.py refuses to ship if they disagree.

questions.question: What does the 'single source for cross-tool distribution' pattern produce?
options: One master AGENTS.md that is manually copied to each tool's config directory
Symlinks (ln -s AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md, .github/copilot-instructions.md, .cursorrules) so one source fans out to all coding agents automatically
A CI job that regenerates tool configs from a central config
A shared cloud storage location that all tools read from
questions.explanation: Single source distribution: use symlinks (ln -s AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md, ln -s AGENTS.md .github/copilot-instructions.md, ln -s AGENTS.md .cursorrules) so all coding agents read from one source of truth. Nx's nx ai-setup automates this across Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini, Codex, OpenCode.

questions.question: What should the uninstall script refuse to do?
options: Remove any files from the target repo
Delete agent_state.json, task_board.json, or outputs/ if they have uncommitted changes — state belongs to the user, not the pack
Run if the pack was not installed by bin/install.sh
Complete if any tests are currently failing
questions.explanation: The uninstaller removes schemas, scripts, docs, and AGENTS.md (with --keep-agents-md opt-out) but refuses to proceed if state files have any uncommitted changes. State belongs to the user — the pack does not own it. Accidental deletion of agent_state.json or task_board.json would be catastrophic.

questions.question: What stays OUT of the agent-workbench-pack?
options: The init script and verification gate
Project-specific tasks, vendor SDK calls, and onboarding prose — these belong in the target repo, not in the portable pack
The schemas and documentation
The feedback runner and handoff generator
questions.explanation: The pack excludes: project-specific tasks (belong on the target repo's board), vendor SDK calls (the pack is framework-agnostic), and onboarding prose (the pack lives next to existing onboarding, not inside it). What stays in: surface schemas, the four scripts, and the four docs.

questions.question: What is SkillKit-style distribution for the workbench pack?
options: Publishing the pack to npm or PyPI
The pack ships as a SkillKit skill (skillkit install agent-workbench-pack) installable across 32 AI agents from a single source
Distributing the pack via email to team members
Publishing the pack as a Docker image
questions.explanation: SkillKit-style distribution: the pack ships as a SkillKit skill installable with skillkit install agent-workbench-pack across 32 AI coding agents from one source. The pack repo is the source of truth; SkillKit is the distribution channel. Vendor lock-in collapses because the seven surfaces stay the same.
